q-15254.name: Question 1
q-15254.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|11-4x|=11-4x,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|11-4x| & =3 \\ 11-4x & =3 \\ -4x & =-8 \\ \frac{-4x}{-4} & =\frac{-8}{-4} \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|11-4x|=-(11-4x),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|11-4x| & =3 \\ -(11-4x) & =3 \\ -11+4x & =3 \\ 4x & =14 \\ \frac{4x}{4} & =\frac{14}{4} \\ x & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=2$ and $x=\frac{7}{2}.$

q-15254.html:
Question 1
?

If |11−4x|=3, then x=

a
27 or 2
b
2 or 72
c
−2 or −27
d
−2 or 72
e
−27 or 2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

  • If |11−4x|=11−4x, we obtain: |11−4x|=311−4x=3−4x=−8−4x−4=−8−4x=2

  • If |11−4x|=−(11−4x), we obtain: |11−4x|=3−(11−4x)=3−11+4x=34x=144x4=144x=72

Therefore, the solutions are x=2 and x=72.

q-15257.name: Question 2
q-15257.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|5x-12|=5x-12,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|5x-12| & =3 \\ 5x-12 & =3 \\ 5x & =15 \\ \frac{5x}{5} & =\frac{15}{5} \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|5x-12|=-(5x-12),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|5x-12| & =3 \\ -(5x-12) & =3 \\ -5x+12 & =3 \\ -5x & =-9 \\ \frac{-5x}{-5} & =\frac{-9}{-5} \\ x & =\frac{9}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=\frac{9}{5}$ and $x=3.$

q-15257.html:
Question 2
?

If |5x−12|=3, then x=

a
−3 or 95
b
−3 or −95
c
1 or 3
d
−1 or 3
e
95 or 3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

  • If |5x−12|=5x−12, we obtain: |5x−12|=35x−12=35x=155x5=155x=3

  • If |5x−12|=−(5x−12), we obtain: |5x−12|=3−(5x−12)=3−5x+12=3−5x=−9−5x−5=−9−5x=95

Therefore, the solutions are x=95 and x=3.

q-154645.name: Question 3
q-154645.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|5-x|=5-x,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|5-x| & =6 \\ 5-x & =6 \\ -x & =1 \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|5-x|=-(5-x),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|5-x| & =6 \\ -(5-x) & =6 \\ -5+x & =6 \\ x & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $x=-1$ and $x=11.$

q-154645.html:
Question 3
?

If |5−x|=6, then x=

a
11 only
b
1 or 5
c
−1 or 11
d
−1 only
e
−11 or −6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

  • If |5−x|=5−x, we obtain: |5−x|=65−x=6−x=1x=−1

  • If |5−x|=−(5−x), we obtain: |5−x|=6−(5−x)=6−5+x=6x=11

Therefore, the solutions are x=−1 and x=11.
